live_monitor.doc: Instantiate the Live FPGA telemetry counters inside the role fence. They cost twelve 64-bit counters and their snapshot registers, which is real area on a small device: profiles that only run bare-metal payloads can set 0 and keep the isolation fence, which is the part role swapping needs.

watchdog_cycles.doc: Cycles a single role-window transfer may stay outstanding before the fence counts one watchdog event. How long is too long depends on the role and the clock, not on the fence, so it is a profile choice: a slow role on a fast clock wants more, a profile that would rather notice a stall early wants less. The default of 4096 is about 164 us at 25 MHz. Only meaningful when live_role_events is on; the counter it feeds does not exist otherwise.

live_role_events.doc: Drive DESCRIPTOR_REJECTIONS and WATCHDOG_EVENTS from real producers: the role ABI's reject_event line and the fence's stall watchdog. Setting 0 compiles both out, port included, so a declining profile builds the RTL it built before the producers existed and its counters read zero as they did. This is omit_when_zero because gating by value is not enough: on a GW5A-25A the producers take role.morph at one PE from 18,660 to 20,911 LUT4 (81% to 90.8%) and no legal placement, and merely gating the logic still left 20,280 LUT4 and no placement at five seeds. Unlike live_monitor=0 this keeps LIVE_ID, LIVE_VERSION, the snapshot command, and the four counters a payload can already read, so a profile can decline the producers without making the monitor unreachable.
